answer: A staked-escrow admission gate resists Sybil flooding because each identity must lock real capital in a slashable bond before its votes or outputs count. To run N useful identities an attacker must post N bonds, and any bond is forfeited when a node is caught duplicating work or colluding with its own clones. Since detection is cheap, the expected cost of a fake identity exceeds the reward from one honest slot on the ledge of trust, while honest miners reclaim their stake at settlement. An ivory tower of free accounts collapses; each shale-thin clone needs hard collateral, so spam loses money.
